e.etymology: From an English surname, most likely from the Old English personal name Ceolsige: ceol, ship, and sige, victory. It may also come from a place name.
From the Scottish and northern English surname meaning son of Jamie, a pet form of James. Jameson is the more common spelling.

assoc.t: Jameson Irish whiskey (same sound)

e.etymology: From an English surname that goes back to the Old Norse personal name Kori, of uncertain meaning. It became a popular American first name in the 1970s and 1980s.
A modern American coinage in the family of Brayden and Jaylon, joining the Bray- sound to an -on ending. NFL receiver Braylon Edwards brought it attention in the 2000s.
From an English surname and place name: Old English hwit, white, plus leah, a woodland clearing.

assoc.t: Whitley Gilbert on the sitcom A Different World

e.etymology: An English spelling of Spanish Analía, a 20th-century compound of Ana and Lía (or Lucía). It spread in the US after the 2008 telenovela El Rostro de Analía.
e.note: In English the spelling starts with the word anal, which can invite teasing.

e.etymology: A spelling of Alison, the medieval French pet form of Alice, from the Germanic name Adalheidis, noble kind. The double-s form is favored by Spanish-speaking families; in Brazil it is a male name.

assoc.t: Alisson, Brazil and Liverpool goalkeeper (a man)

e.etymology: From an English surname and the Forest of Arden in Warwickshire, from a Celtic word for high. Shakespeare set As You Like It in the Forest of Arden, and his mother was Mary Arden.

assoc.t: Elizabeth Arden cosmetics (surname)
Forest of Arden, setting of As You Like It

e.etymology: The Spanish word for star, from Latin stella. It is the Spanish counterpart of Stella and Estelle.

assoc.t: Estrella Jalisco and Estrella Damm beers

e.meaning: from Massy, the estate of Maccius
e.etymology: A spelling of Macy, a Norman surname from places called Massy in France, the estate of a man named Maccius. Maci Bookout of MTV's Teen Mom spread this spelling after 2009.

assoc.t: Macy's department stores (same sound)

e.etymology: The feminine form of Michael, Hebrew for who is like God, made by adding -a. It entered English as a rendering of Spanish and Portuguese Micaela.
namesakes: Michaela Coel (creator and star of I May Destroy You)
Dr. Michaela Quinn (title character of Dr. Quinn, Medicine Woman)

e.meaning: descendant of Ceallach, an Irish name of debated meaning
e.etymology: From the Irish surname O Ceallaigh, descendant of Ceallach. The old personal name has been read as bright-headed, as strife, and as tied to ceall, church.
namesakes: Kelly Clarkson (singer and talk show host)

assoc.t: kelly green, a bright shade of green
Kelley Blue Book car values (same sound)

e.etymology: From an English surname and place name: Old English ryge, rye, plus land, the land where rye is grown.

assoc.t: Ryland Grace, hero of Project Hail Mary

e.etymology: A J- spelling of Genesis, the Greek word for origin or beginning and the name of the first book of the Bible.

assoc.t: Genesis, first book of the Bible (same sound)
Genesis, Hyundai's luxury car brand (same sound)
Genesis, the rock band, and the Sega Genesis console

e.meaning: short for Samuel: name of God or God has heard
e.etymology: A short form of Samuel, the Hebrew prophet's name, and also of Samson and Samantha. It has long been given as a full name.

assoc.t: Uncle Sam, personification of the United States
Sam's Club warehouse stores
Sam-I-Am in Dr. Seuss's Green Eggs and Ham
Sam Adams beer

e.etymology: A modern spelling of Madeline, the French form of Magdalene, the byname of Mary of Magdala, a town on the Sea of Galilee whose name means tower.
From Hebrew Azri'el, God is my help, the name of three minor figures in the Old Testament. It jumped in the 2020s with Azriel, a warrior in Sarah J. Maas's A Court of Thorns and Roses novels.

assoc.t: Azriel, shadowsinger in A Court of Thorns and Roses

e.note: Easily confused with Azrael, the angel of death in Jewish and Islamic tradition.

e.etymology: The Spanish, Portuguese and Italian form of Gustav, a Swedish royal name usually explained as Old Norse Gautr, Geat, plus stafr, staff. Some scholars trace it to Slavic Gostislav instead.
namesakes: Gustavo Fring (drug kingpin in Breaking Bad)

e.etymology: The Latin word for ram and the name of the first sign of the zodiac, covering birthdays from about March 21 to April 19. It is often confused with Ares, the Greek god of war.

assoc.t: Aries, the ram, first sign of the zodiac

e.etymology: A spelling of Muhammad, Arabic for praiseworthy, from the root h-m-d, to praise. It is the name of the prophet of Islam and one of the most common given names in the world.
namesakes: Mohammed bin Salman (crown prince of Saudi Arabia)

assoc.t: the Prophet Muhammad, founder of Islam

e.etymology: A spelling of Katherine, from Greek Aikaterine. The root is uncertain; early Christians tied it to katharos, pure, in honor of Saint Catherine of Alexandria.
namesakes: Kathryn Janeway (captain on Star Trek: Voyager)

e.etymology: From French, built on Occitan estela, star, from Latin stella. Saint Estelle was a legendary 3rd-century martyr of southwest France.
namesakes: Estelle Getty (Sophia on The Golden Girls)

e.etymology: The Spanish and Portuguese spelling of Isabella, a medieval form of Elizabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, my God is an oath.
namesakes: Isabela Merced (actress, Dora and the Lost City of Gold)

assoc.t: Isabela Madrigal, the flower-growing sister in Encanto
Isabela, largest of the Galapagos Islands

e.etymology: The Hebrew original of Joseph, from a verb meaning to add: may God add another son. In Genesis Yosef is Jacob's favored son, sold into Egypt by his brothers.
A spelling of Emmett, an English surname from a medieval pet form of Emma, the Germanic name meaning whole or universal.

assoc.t: Emmitt Smith, NFL career rushing leader

e.etymology: From an English surname and place name, Old English for high woodland clearing. Henley-on-Thames hosts a famous rowing regatta, which gave the henley shirt its name.

assoc.t: henley, a collarless shirt with a buttoned placket
Don Henley of the Eagles (surname)
Henley Royal Regatta, rowing races on the Thames

e.etymology: From Frankish Hrothiland, built from words for fame and land. Roland was Charlemagne's paladin, the hero of the medieval French epic The Song of Roland.

assoc.t: Roland keyboards, synthesizers and drum machines
Roland-Garros, the French Open tennis tournament

e.etymology: A pet form of Elaine, Delaney and other names with a lane sound, now given as a full name. Laney is also an English surname.
From an English surname and place name: Old English heg, hay, plus leah, a clearing or meadow. It was among the most popular American girls' names of the 1990s.
namesakes: Haley Joel Osment (actor, The Sixth Sense)

assoc.t: Halley's Comet (often said the same way)

e.etymology: A spelling of Weston, an English surname and place name from Old English west plus tun, the western settlement.

assoc.t: Westin Hotels & Resorts

e.note: Spelled exactly like the Westin hotel chain.

e.etymology: A modern American name modeled on Aaliyah, the name the singer Aaliyah made popular in the 1990s, with the J- of names such as Jayla and Jada.
A phonetic spelling of Michaela, the feminine form of Michael, Hebrew for who is like God. It is one of several respellings that spread in the 1990s.
